start.text: {pet} finds a tiny paper star beside the window. “I wonder where you belong?” A silver trail leads into an imaginary night sky.

trail.text: The trail ends at a cloud. The star is quiet. {pet} sits beside it. “We can work this out together.”

moon.text: The moon glows softly. “Some stars belong in the sky. Some belong in a home full of stories.” {pet} looks at the little paper star.

choices.label: Make a home on our wall
Ask the star what it likes

map.text: You draw a map full of dots. The little star points to a window. It looks just like yours!

song.text: Your quiet song sounds like home. The star twinkles toward the window. “Perhaps home is where we feel welcome,” says {pet}.

ask.text: The star gives a tiny rustle. It wants to be near your pictures. {pet} smiles. “We remembered to listen.”

choices.label: Find a place on our wall

home.text: You hang the star near your art. It was a pretend journey, but the kindness was real. “Welcome home,” whispers {pet}.

start.text: On an imaginary beach, {pet} spots a beautiful shell. A tiny crab is resting beside it. “Shall we look closer?”

watch.text: You notice the crab slowly moving toward the shell. Maybe this is its home. {pet} waits with you.

hello.text: “Hello, little neighbour,” says {pet}. The crab pauses. You leave plenty of room so it can choose where to go.

choices.label: Make a picture of the beach

space.text: The crab settles beside the shell. You sit a little further away and listen to the pretend waves. Sometimes helping means giving space.

draw.text: You make a shell shape in the sand. “We can keep a picture and leave the beach as we found it,” says {pet}.

end.text: The shell stays on the beach. You take a lovely memory home. {pet} remembers how carefully you watched and listened.

stories.title: The seed that took its time
stories.subtitle: Nature · Patience · 4 minutes

start.text: {pet} finds a little seed in our story garden. “What could this become?” You tuck it gently into soil.

water.text: The soil is gently damp. Now our seed needs sunlight and time. Nothing changes straight away, and that is okay.

choices.label: Make a picture while we wait
Tell the seed a gentle story

sun.text: A warm patch of light reaches the pot. You add a little water. “Growing takes its own time,” says {pet}.

choices.label: Make a picture while we wait
Tell the seed a gentle story

wait.text: In our story, several days pass. You draw what you imagine the plant might look like. Then one morning, a tiny green shoot appears.

story.text: You tell a story about a giant garden. Several story-days pass. The plant grows slowly, with soil, light, water and time.

end.text: The shoot is small and wonderful. {pet} smiles. “Small beginnings count.” You keep a memory of the seed that grew in its own time.

start.text: A huge dinosaur shadow stretches across the pretend garden. {pet} pauses. The shadow looks tall, but its feet are very small.

left.text: You move around the paper tree. The shadow becomes shorter. A little hatchling is standing beside a lantern. “I thought I looked enormous,” it says.

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

right.text: “Hello,” says {pet} softly. A tiny voice answers, “I was trying to look brave.” A hatchling steps out, carrying a paper leaf.

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

one.text: You move the pretend light and watch the shadow change. Big shadows can belong to little things. The hatchling invents a shadow dance for you.

two.text: You sit together without asking the hatchling to be bigger or louder. Soon it shares its leaf. Being welcome feels better than looking enormous.

end.text: The three friends make a tiny shadow theatre. {pet} remembers that looking again—and listening—can change a scary first guess.

start.text: {pet} finds an empty envelope in the pretend rocket. “What would the moon like to hear?” The window is full of quiet stars.

left.text: You draw the moon with a cosy scarf. A passing comet laughs gently. “That looks warm! But how will the moon know who sent it?”

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

right.text: You choose the words “Thank you for lighting our pretend journey.” A little star offers to carry the message, but first it needs a safe place to fold it.

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

one.text: Your envelope becomes a pretend moonboat. You test it on a blanket sea. It tips once, so you fold a wider base and try again.

two.text: The comet slows down to listen. Together you make a delivery map with three stars and a crescent. Asking for help becomes part of the adventure.

end.text: The moon sends back a silver paper dot. It has no price and earns no points. It simply reminds {pet} of something kind you made together.

start.text: Under a blanket ocean, a young whale has forgotten the last note of its song. {pet} can hear three gentle sounds: hum, splash, hum.

choices.label: Ask the whale how it feels

left.text: You wait through a quiet pause. Another hum arrives. The whale smiles: the song was not broken. It had a space for breathing.

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

right.text: “I feel rushed,” says the whale. {pet} sits on a pretend sea rock. “We can wait. Your song belongs to you.”

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

one.text: You move your hands like slow waves. The whale joins when it is ready. Your rhythms are different, and they still fit together.

two.text: Nobody fills the silence. At last the whale adds a small new note. It sounds different from yesterday, and that is all right.

end.text: The blanket ocean becomes quiet again. {pet} keeps a memory of listening patiently, and of a song that had room for everyone.

stories.title: The fox with the blue picture
stories.topic: the fox with the blue picture
stories.subtitle: Animals · A story together

start.text: A little fox paints a blue sun. Another animal says suns should be yellow. The fox turns its picture face down. {pet} notices.

left.text: “It is the sun in my dream,” says the fox. In that dream the sky is peach and the grass is silver. {pet} wants to hear more.

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

right.text: You draw a purple leaf beside the fox. “Pictures can show things we imagine too,” says {pet}. The fox peeks at the paper.

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

one.text: Each friend makes a different dream picture. You leave spaces between them so every picture has a home. No one chooses a winner.

two.text: You ask, “What happens in your dream?” The fox tells a story about cool blue sunshine. The other animal listens and sees the picture differently.

end.text: The blue sun goes on the pretend gallery wall. {pet} remembers that curiosity can make room for ideas that are different from our own.

stories.title: The seed that took its time
stories.topic: the seed that took its time
stories.subtitle: Nature · A story together

start.text: In an imaginary garden, {pet} plants a paper seed beside a tall flower. Nothing happens at once. “Perhaps this seed has its own pace,” says {pet}.

left.text: You notice a tiny bend in the pretend soil. It is easy to miss beside the tall flower. The garden has many kinds of growing.

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

right.text: You draw a sun, a water drop and a clock. The plan leaves time to wait. {pet} puts away the measuring stick: this is not a race.

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

one.text: You imagine two little leaves reaching up. They do not have to look exactly like the tall flower. You give the seed a hopeful name.

two.text: You watch a paper butterfly and notice the leaf shapes nearby. There are things to enjoy while something new is growing.

end.text: Later in your pretend story, the seed becomes a sprout. {pet} keeps your care-plan picture as a memory of patience, not of being first.

start.text: A pretend stream divides the dinosaur picnic. A longneck steps across, but a tiny hatchling cannot. {pet} looks at their very different feet.

left.text: “I need stones closer together,” says the hatchling. You make room for its idea. The longneck offers to carry pretend building blocks.

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

right.text: You build a model on the rug. One gap is too wide for a little toy foot. Finding the gap gives you a useful clue.

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

one.text: The new stone makes two small steps instead of one enormous jump. The hatchling chooses to try, and the friends wait nearby.

two.text: You make a broad path from flat blocks. There is room for different feet and different speeds. Nobody needs to hurry.

end.text: Everyone reaches the imaginary picnic. {pet} remembers that a good path can change to welcome more friends.

stories.title: The map with an empty space
stories.topic: the map with an empty space
stories.subtitle: Space · A story together

start.text: The pretend star map has an empty corner. {pet} wonders whether a missing mark means the map is wrong—or whether there is more to discover.

left.text: The traveller says, “I have only seen part of the sky.” Its map is useful, but it is not everything. {pet} leaves room for a new idea.

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

right.text: Three stars make a triangle you have not noticed before. You trace it with a finger. Looking slowly reveals a new path.

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

one.text: You draw your route with a dotted line to show it is a guess. A guess can help you explore without pretending you already know.

two.text: You add a friendly question mark. “We can wonder about something without solving it today,” says {pet}.

end.text: The map returns to your room with a little more detail and plenty of open space. {pet} remembers how you made room for curiosity.

start.text: An otter tries to carry six pretend pebbles in one paw. Plop! They tumble onto the rug. {pet} sits down to think beside it.

choices.label: Look for something to carry them

left.text: The otter carries two pebbles, then comes back. It takes more trips, but the pebbles stay safe. A smaller step can work well.

choices.label: Ask friends to share the trips

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

right.text: You find a paper basket with a loose handle. It could help, but first you examine where the handle bends.

choices.label: Ask friends to share the trips

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

one.text: You fold a wider handle and test it with one pretend pebble before adding more. The otter likes testing an idea in small steps.

two.text: Each friend chooses a little load. Nobody has to carry the same amount. Together they bring the pebbles to the pretend shore.

end.text: The otter makes a pebble picture for everyone. {pet} remembers that trying another way and sharing work are both clever choices.

start.text: The pretend garden looks golden where it looked green before. {pet} finds no spilled paint. The paper sun is lower in the sky.

left.text: You hold a pretend leaf near the warm paper sun, then in the shade. The leaf has not changed into a new leaf, but it looks different.

choices.label: Draw two versions of the garden

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

right.text: A butterfly says the garden looks different at different times. “Perhaps we can notice it together,” says {pet}.

choices.label: Draw two versions of the garden

interaction.label: Touch our discovery
interaction.message: A little clue to remember together.

one.text: One picture shows a bright morning, the other a gentle evening. Both belong to the same garden. You choose colours that tell each story.

two.text: You put a leaf shape and a sunshine mark in your book. There is space for another observation on another day, with a grown-up nearby.

end.text: The colour mystery becomes a question to enjoy. {pet} keeps your picture and suggests looking for changing light in your own room sometime.

stories.title: Milo and the Missing Moonlight
stories.subtitle: A lantern, two paths, one lovely discovery

opening.text: The moon’s silver path has vanished. Let’s light our lantern and look together!

interaction.label: Light the lantern
interaction.message: A warm little glow!

tree.text: A firefly is tangled in a curled leaf. Tap the leaf to help it unfold.

interaction.label: Unfold the leaf
interaction.message: The firefly is free!

pond.text: The pond holds a tiny silver shimmer. Touch the water gently to find its source.

interaction.label: Touch the shimmer
interaction.message: Ripples point toward the clouds!

firefly.text: Our new friend lights a path to the hill. The moon is hiding behind a cloud!

interaction.label: Find the hidden moon
interaction.message: There you are!

cloud.text: A soft cloud floats across the moon. Trace a breeze with your finger, or tap the cloud.

interaction.label: Make a gentle breeze
interaction.message: The clouds drift apart!

tree-ending.text: Moonlight fills the garden. We found the moon—and made a firefly friend. Let’s keep a glowing memory.

interaction.label: Catch a pretend sparkle
interaction.message: Our firefly lantern keepsake

pond-ending.text: A silver path sparkles across the pond. We looked carefully and found our answer together.

interaction.label: Keep a pretend moonbeam
interaction.message: Our silver moonbeam keepsake

How could we find out more without blaming anyone?

responses.Red: Red and blue paint can make purple.
responses.Yellow: Yellow and blue paint can make green.

rounds.prompt: How light shall our pretend green become?

responses.A little white: White paint makes a lighter green.
responses.More white: More white paint makes a paler green.

responses.Far: Moving our light farther away makes this shadow smaller.

rounds.prompt: Where shall our pretend light shine from?

responses.Left: The shadow falls away from the light, to the right.
responses.Right: The shadow falls to the left.

rounds.prompt: Can light pass through our pretend object?

responses.Clear glass: Clear glass lets much of the light through.
responses.Cardboard: Cardboard blocks light and makes a dark shadow.

rounds.prompt: Choose something for our digital pond.

responses.Cork: Our cork floats. It is less dense than water.
responses.Stone: Our solid stone sinks. It is denser than water.

rounds.prompt: Try two shapes made from the same pretend clay.

responses.Hollow boat: A wide hollow clay boat can float by pushing aside enough water.

rounds.prompt: What might change our pretend boat?

responses.Add weight: Enough extra weight makes our boat sink.

rounds.prompt: Give our pretend seed a little water.

responses.A few drops: Water helps a seed begin to grow.
responses.Notice the seed: A seed holds the beginning of a plant.

rounds.prompt: Our seed has roots and a shoot. Look closely.

responses.Roots: Roots take up water and hold the plant in place.
responses.Shoot: The shoot grows towards the light.

rounds.prompt: Our pretend leaves have opened.

responses.Light: Green leaves use light to help the plant make food.
responses.Time: Real plants grow slowly. Our pretend garden skips ahead.

rounds.prompt: Choose an object for our digital magnet.

responses.Iron nail: Iron is attracted to our magnet. This nail stays on screen.
responses.Wood: Wood is not attracted to the magnet.

rounds.prompt: Try another pretend material.

responses.Steel clip: Many steel clips are attracted to magnets.
responses.Plastic: Plastic is not attracted to our magnet.

rounds.prompt: Bring two pretend magnet ends together.
Where can our pretend puddle water go?

responses.Into the air: Some liquid water becomes water vapour in the air.
responses.Stay a while: Some water stays in the puddle while other water evaporates.

rounds.prompt: Higher up, water vapour cools.

responses.Make droplets: Tiny liquid droplets can gather into clouds.
responses.Look at clouds: Clouds contain tiny water droplets or ice crystals.

rounds.prompt: The cloud’s drops grow heavier.

responses.Rain: Water falls as rain and gathers again.
responses.Follow a stream: Streams can carry water towards lakes and the sea.

rounds.prompt: Leaf, pebble, leaf, pebble… what could come next?

responses.Leaf: A leaf continues our repeating pair.
responses.Flower: A flower starts a new pattern. We can invent one too.

rounds.prompt: Look at our pretend butterfly wings.

responses.Left wing: The two sides have matching shapes.
responses.Right wing: Many butterfly wing patterns are roughly symmetrical.

rounds.prompt: Make a pattern with Milo.

responses.Big, small: Big, small, big, small: a repeating size pattern.
responses.Round, long: Round, long, round, long: a repeating shape pattern.
